OpenHD Glide RKMPP packaged-header injection reproduction
=========================================================

Device: Orange Pi 5 / RK3588, kernel 5.10.160-1
Date: 2026-07-30

Isolation:
- openhd-glide.service stopped and runtime-masked
- p401-openhd-bridge.service stopped and runtime-masked
- p401-direct-daemon.service stopped and runtime-masked
- no KMS, GlideUI, Flow, MAVLink, or Artosyn process
- input: p401-midstream-no-idr.rtp replayed directly to UDP/5600

Probe:
  glide-rkmpp-rtp-probe --duration 30 --stats-ms 250 \
    --debug-inject-x20-header

Replay:
  python3 tools/artosyn_rtp_fixture.py replay \
    testdata/artosyn/p401-midstream-no-idr.rtp \
    192.168.7.186 --cycles 1 --packet-delay-us 500

Last output streamed over SSH before reset:

  [WARN] DEBUG ONLY: injecting packaged X20 header before first H264 access unit
  [INFO] first native RKMPP DMABUF layout fmt=0x0 width=1280 height=720
         hstride=1280 vstride=720 buffer_size=1843200 fd=9
         drm_format=NV12 luma_height=720 offset_uv=921600
  probe_frames=2 parsed_units=3 submitted_packets=3 decoded_frames=2
         rtp_packets=32 x20_header_injections=1 submit_stalls=0
  probe_frames=2 parsed_units=7 submitted_packets=7 decoded_frames=2
         rtp_packets=107 x20_header_injections=1 submit_stalls=1

The SSH connection and ICMP reachability then disappeared immediately.

Boot ID before replay:
  86901d8b-eb39-42eb-ae4f-af2ba139c3e7

Boot ID after the board returned:
  3304afde-b710-4a6e-82f1-4b4cac2e02e2

Finding at time of capture:
The packaged-header path produced two decoded frames, then entered an RKMPP
submit stall and hard-reset the board. The reset reproduced without any
Artosyn hardware process or Glide rendering/composition process.

Subsequent FPVue comparison:
- FPVue packages the identical 692-byte x20_header.h264.
- That file contains an IDR and two P-frames in addition to parameter sets.
- FPVue provisions 16 external DRM output buffers on MPP info-change before
  acknowledging MPP_DEC_SET_INFO_CHANGE_READY.
- Glide acknowledged info-change without provisioning that output pool and
  retained the currently scanned-out MppFrame.

Follow-up A/B results (2026-07-31):
- A 16-buffer internal DMA output group decoded all three seed frames but the
  access-unit feed still stalled and reset the board.
- Reusing one persistent MppPacket also stalled and reset the board.
- FPVue itself, built from its openhd branch on this Orange Pi, accepted this
  fixture with --x20-force and kept the same boot ID.
- Glide changed from RTP-timestamp access-unit aggregation to FPVue-style
  Annex-B NAL submission while retaining the 16-buffer output group.
- One fixture cycle decoded 105 frames with zero stalls and no reboot.
- Five fixture cycles sent 2,000 RTP packets / 656 NAL submissions, decoded
  521 frames, reported zero submit stalls, and kept boot ID
  b9a5113a-dc4d-4ace-be86-8419d2ac7cb3 unchanged.

Conclusion:
The reboot trigger was the combination of the X20 seed and Glide's aggregated
access-unit MPP packets. FPVue's NAL-aligned feed is stable on the same board,
seed, and captured mid-GOP input. The production H.264/H.265 RKMPP path now
submits complete NALs independently.
